references.text: The seventh day shall be a holy convocation, and no work shall be done. This is the original ordinance concerning the last day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
Confirms that the seventh day shall be a feast to the Lord during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
Parallel text in Leviticus describing the first and seventh days of the Feast of Unleavened Bread as holy convocations where no work is to be done.
Moses repeats the ordinance concerning the seventh day as a festive assembly for the Lord where no work shall be done.
The first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread has the same ordinance regarding a holy convocation and prohibition of work, forming the framework around the feast.
The Sabbath commandment establishing the principle of rest from work on holy days.
